This is from Markepedia..

The CanCan

Very often price will move into, or even better, break out of a zone with strong momentum, creating a pole.

Usually a pole will have a flag on top, gathering orders for price to avance.

But if the flag breaks back into the pole, this is a significant turn in value.

A CanCan can often occur at such an event.

Price moves hard, flags briefly, and moves back quickly with a Liquidity Spike. This liquidity spike will mean there may very well be orders left to be filled at the edge of the flag, so you'll very often see compression back towards it, with extra orders being hidden, so that when price hits the cap, it can shoot back through the compression and on to the base of the pole.

Hi Gristar,

I know it is really easy to look at things in hindsight, but I thought it would be a good exercise. The following is just my opinion which could be totally off, but here goes…. First off, I believe the cap of the RBD/DBR should be a clean one i.e. no CP. In this case the top was clearly CPed. When price got to the last standing supply in the CP it did react; down to the next important zone (It could have been traded around E, better seen on M15). Point 1 in H4 is demand & 2 also but in M30.

If you look at H1, you’ll see the important zone I was referring to earlier… it is a FL with 1 acting as its FTR. You’ll also notice that it was also a nice SR flip. For me had the FTR been ENG and price returned to the area around E, I would have definitely taken the risk… but nothing major was engulfed (major meaning non-local). The yellow ellipse is the decision to break into CP, better seen on LTFs.

Looking into M5 and supposing I really still wanted to trade this; one setup was available after the pink line got ENG & price returned to the FTR in the pink rectangle, resulting in a small loss. All the other important lows in green did not get ENG. And once we broke out of the last Supply of CP, it was over.

Hope this helps

Making a start on my QM Can Can homework. Just wanted to clarify something before I do too many. In Markepedia, IF's examples are Can Can reversals. However, many examples posted in this thread are Can Can trend continuation setups. My question is can Can Can setups be both reversals and continuations?

Here's my 1st Can Can

I think they can be both continuation and reversals.

For the Bearish Can Can The move of a pole up and flagging on top and instead of another pole up, it breaks down south with a pole down creating a price cap. That's where orders are sitting, and a compression up to the capped supply is clearing out little pockets of demand to bring the price further.
